title: Collecting and processing single-particle cryo-EM data with tilts
protocol: Prepare all sample grids according to conventional single-particle cryo-EM analysis protocols.
Use gold grids instead of carbon grids for superior results.
Perform vitrification steps identically for holey carbon and holey gold grids, noting that blotting times are generally shorter with gold grids.
Observe differences in particle concentration and extent of preferred particle orientation based on specimen type.
Place the grid into the microscope to begin data collection.
Determine the correct eucentric height for the square on the grid.
Adjust the stage alpha parameter to tilt the stage to the desired angle.
Acquire a low-magnification square image at the tilted position.
Queue up holes in the designated area of the low-magnification image.
Collect high-magnification images from the queued locations at the specified tilt angle.
Perform per-particle CTF estimation for each micrograph.
Use GCTF software to estimate CTF values locally within each particle.
Run GCTF with options \(-apix, -kV, -cs, -ac, -dstep\) and additional tilt-specific options: \(-do_local_refine 1\), \(-do_validation 1\).
Specify the box suffix as either .box or .star in the command.
Assume all micrographs are located in a directory named "Micrographs".
Perform 2D classification using per-particle defocus values as input.
Carry out 3D classification with conventional processing methods and per-particle defocus values.
Execute 3D refinement using standard procedures and input of per-particle defocus values.
Evaluate the degree of preferred orientation by analyzing Euler angle distribution.
Assess directional resolution anisotropy quantitatively using 3DFSC software.
Download 3DFSC from its repository for anisotropy analysis.
